questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

We has travelled / to many states / of India to get / an essence of its diversity.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the incorrect usage of the verb "**has**" instead of "**have**" in "**We has travelled**."
 
• The subject "**We**" requires the verb "**have**" to be grammatically correct.
 
• The correct phrase should be "**We have travelled**," ensuring grammatical correctness and clarity.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **Option 2** of the sentence.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"**We have travelled** to many states of India to get an essence of its diversity."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1: "an essence of its diversity" **– This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **3: "to many states"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **4: "of India to get"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.

questions.question:
Select the option that corrects the following sentence.

All tickets of the FIFA World Cup have been sold away.

options.text: All tickets of the FIFA World Cup have been sold among.
All tickets of the FIFA World Cup have been sold out.
All tickets of the FIFA World Cup have been sold into.
All tickets of the FIFA World Cup have been sold across.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the use of the phrase "**sold away**" which is incorrect in this context.
 
• The correct phrase should be "**sold out**" which means that all tickets have been purchased.
 
• The phrase **"sold away" **is not commonly used in English and does not convey the intended meaning.
 
• Thus, the error is corrected by replacing **"sold away"** with **"sold out".**
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"All tickets of the FIFA World Cup have been **sold out.**"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "sold among" **– This phrase is incorrect and does not fit the context of the sentence.
 
• **Option 3: "sold into"** – This phrase is incorrect and does not fit the context of the sentence.
 
• **Option 4: "sold across"** – This phrase is incorrect and does not fit the context of the sentence.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The captain dropped the trophy while he ________the victory with his teammates.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence requires **the past continuous tense to indicate an action that was ongoing at the time another action occurred.**
 
• The **past continuous tense** is formed using **"was/were" + the present participle (verb + -ing).**
 
• In this case, **"was celebrating" **correctly indicates that the celebration was in progress when the trophy was dropped.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The captain dropped the trophy while he **was celebrating** the victory with his teammates."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "celebrated"** – This is the simple past tense, which does not convey the ongoing nature of the action.
 
• **Option 3: "is celebrating"** – This is the present continuous tense, which is not appropriate for past events.
 
• **Option 4: "celebrates"** – This is the simple present tense, which is not appropriate for past events.

questions.question:

Employers in many developing countries report that a lack of skilled workers is a major and increasing bottleneck for their operations, __affected their capacity__ to innovate.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the incorrect form of the verb "**affected**."
 
• The correct form should be "**affecting**" to properly convey the ongoing impact on their capacity to innovate.
 
• The revised phrase should be "**affecting their capacity**," ensuring grammatical correctness and clarity.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Employers in many developing countries report that a lack of skilled workers is a major and increasing bottleneck for their operations, **affecting **their capacity to innovate."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "effect their capacity"** – This option is incorrect as "effect" is a noun, not a verb. The sentence requires a verb.
 
• **Option 3: "effecting their capacity"** – This option is incorrect because "effect" as a verb means to bring about or cause, which does not fit the context.
 
• **Option 4: "affect their capacity"** – This option is incorrect because it does not fit the sentence structure that requires a present participle form.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.

The United Nations is working to eliminate __the vicious cycle__ of poverty.
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"vicious cycle"** means a sequence of reciprocal cause and effect in which two or more elements intensify and aggravate each other, leading to a worsening situation. (दुष्चक्र)

 
 
• **Example: **The family was trapped in a **vicious cycle** of debt and poverty.
 
 
 
• **"Vicious cycle"** refers to a situation where one problem causes another, which then makes the original problem worse, creating a loop of negative outcomes. (दुष्चक्र)
 
 
• **Example: **Lack of education leads to unemployment, which leads to poverty, and poverty leads to lack of education, forming a** vicious cycle.**
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the phrase **'vicious cycle' **means **'one problem causes another'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Example:** The company exploited a loophole in the tax law to avoid paying taxes.
 
 
 
• **The barrier of poverty** (गरीबी की बाधा): An obstacle that prevents progress or achievement, specifically related to poverty.
